marta: quick note 0: saw p99 tail in continuous-batcher for ~3m. tenant 'alpha' burst appears causal. thoughts on queue ownership vs soft-reserve?

kieran: numbers?
marta: p50 ~11ms; p99 jumped 110 -> 820ms; enqueue wait logs show long stalls (queue_len ~60).

joy: two high-level paths: 1) per-tenant micro-lanes (hard isolation, risk fragmentation) 2) shared lanes + soft-reserve/headroom tickets (keeps packing).

ben: pro/con quick list:
- micro-lanes: clear SLO boundaries, complex compaction needed, telemetry cost
- soft-reserve: preserves packing, needs deterministic eviction and ticket regen tuning

kieran: telemetry gap: lane-level histograms missing. we'll need compact metrics before rollout.

joy: propose "burst-ticket" bucket per tenant: tokens consumed by short bursts, regen at controlled rate. when bucket empty, tenant falls back to standard fair admission (no starve).

ben: eviction: add deadline_bias to coalesce score (score = deadline_hint / est_tokens * deadline_bias_factor). prefer small-deadline/high-score reqs. token estimates from heuristics (model + input_len). log mis-orders.

derek: rollout plan: behind FF, telemetry + canary. enable tickets for 5-10% high-burst tenants. guardrails: rollback if p99 > 2x baseline or GPU occupancy drop > 12% or packing loss > 10%.

marta: if soft-reserve fails, fallback = limited micro-lane cohort with auto-compaction (merge cold lanes after idle window). keep API surface unchanged.

ops-bot: incident IN-2026-03-22-11 opened for p99.

marta: action items: kieran - telemetry schema + dashboards; joy - simulator for ticket tuning; ben - eviction/order draft and invariants; derek - canary runbook + rollback. sync in tomorrow's runtime sync.
